narrative:
On September 8, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 51.4%, taking up 1,386 of the 2,696 scheduled matters across 44 judges. This marks an improvement over the preceding day's rate of 48.5% (1,400 heard of 2,884 scheduled) and sustains an upward trajectory compared to previous sessions on August 18 (43.3%) and August 12 (40.2%). 

Judicial clearance exhibited notable variation across court halls. Justice C.M. Poonacha in Hall 31 managed the heaviest individual list, hearing 123 of 174 scheduled cases (70.7%). Justice E.S. Indiresh in Hall 18 demonstrated strong disposal efficiency, hearing 65 of 79 matters (82.3%), while Justice V. Srishananda in Hall 23 cleared 78 of 123 cases (63.4%) on his primary list and 28 of 30 (93.3%) on a secondary roster. In contrast, several benches experienced reduced throughput, including Hall 14, where Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum took up 20 of 77 matters (26.0%), and Hall 24, where Justice Hanchate Sanjeevkumar heard 21 of 89 cases (23.6%).

Disposal patterns diverged sharply across procedural stages. Preliminary hearings achieved the highest conversion among major stages at 60.5% (279 of 461), followed by orders at 55.7% (456 of 819) and admissions at 54.0% (434 of 804). Both orders and admissions saw slight drops from September 7 rates of 58.8% and 62.8%, respectively. Final hearings remained a key procedural bottleneck, converting just 28.8% (142 of 493
), down from 32.5% the prior day. 

Writ petitions comprised the largest case category, accounting for 1,135 scheduled cases with a clearance rate of 52.9% (600 heard), up significantly from 44.4% on September 7. Criminal petitions reached 55.7% (258 of 463), though declining from 65.9% yesterday. Regular first appeals faced low clearance at 20.5% (23 of 112), whereas criminal appeals saw robust progress at 68.1% (79 of 116).
